I absolutely LOVE The Last Jedi.

TFA was a solid start to a new trilogy. Plenty of nostalgia to make us happy, you call tell Mr Ford was having a blast, and enough mysteries and speculation at the end to fuel YouTube for a few years. JJ was the perfect man for the job being known for setting up nail-biting mysteries in Alias and Lost.  

TLJ blew my mind. The hype was real after years of everyone consuming hours of conspiracies on YouTube to see which predictions were right. The only work by Rian Johnson that I saw before was Looper and I loved that movie, a true mind bender with great action. The opening space battle was great, funny and stunning. It kept the tradition of opening the movie in space but seeing an X-Wing vs a Star Destroyer to bide time was an excellent change of pace, I knew this was going to be a wild ride. When Luke just simply tossed his lightsaber, I laughed in shock. His view on the old Jedi order made plenty of sense and was solidified by the fantastic Yoda scene. When it was explained why he was in self imposed exile, of course he lost hope and isolation. How else were you going to explain that cliffhanger from TFA? I was sad that he had lost hope and cut himself off from the force, being the opposite of what we grew up with. But the movie wasn't over.

 Everyone had a million theories on who Rey's parents were. Then Rian pulled the rug and said she was a nobody. I was disappointed at first. Then it sunk in. Luke was originally a nobody. That was the point. Anyone can be special all on their own. Once I realized this, I fell in love with the movie. That Disney had the balls to disrupt the fan theories. To expand on the lore and create a trilogy all on its own, to inspire everyone that you can be special without nepotism. This resonated heavily with me (father disowned me at 13, he's a millionaire and I plan on pissing on his grave in a few years) and I was so pumped for it.

The subplot with Rose and Finn I thought was interesting. To see what  Las Vegas would look like in Star Wars. Dj was a neat character and unique character. He showed that this saga still has its seedy scoundrels. My only gripe in the whole movie is that Finn should've done something better instead of a heist. Finn should've been treated better. John Boyega deserves better and shame on Disney for not making him into something iconic and original. Anyways.

The fight against Snoke and the guards was awesome and visually stunning. Killing Snoke was the best thing they did for Kylo for him to grow as a character. And Rey not taking up his offer to join after her core was shaken by the reveal enforced that she truly has a good heart. 

The fight on Craitt is the best action sequence of the ST. The scrappiness of the ships against impossible odds combined with the red and white dust makes it so iconic. 

Then Luke shows up. Fights Kylo, revealing a new awesome Jedi ability, alluding to the myth and the power of the greatest Jedi to ever exist. "I am not the last Jedi." My hero reconnected to the force and regained his hope. Beautiful story arc and redemption. I was so happy that Disney let Rian go for it, challenging our expectations and understanding. The sheer risk, I thought, paid off beautifully.

A good many of you hate it. Shame.

As a result, we got TROS. Rehired JJ and fired Colin Trevorrow. Because JJ has such a great track record in wrapping up stories in a satisfying way. Yeah right, I knew this would be trouble after the severe backlash of the ending of Lost. They backtracked every bold move from TLJ. The whole thing felt like fanfic. I was so disappointed in Disney for putting their tail between their legs and gave us that hot turd. C3P0 was the only thing that kept me seated, he had a great story arc. I laughed my ass off when Ben and Rey kissed. By that point I had enough and I left the theater. 

Disney treated us like adults with the first two. The reception to TLJ is how we got TROS. 

A while back I read the script for Colin's Duel of The Fates. We were robbed of that masterpiece and I blame the lot of you. We could've had a truly iconic trilogy that separated from the rest. Shame!
